newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says it killed two guerrillas in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israel says it killed two guerrillas in Lebanon.

text.p: The Israeli army said on Tuesday its soldiers killed two Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas and wounded a number of others in a raid north of the Jewish state's occupation zone in Lebanon.

"At least two terrorists were killed and a number were wounded when an army force working north of the security zone in the area of the village Ghandouriyeh hit a terrorist unit of the Hizbollah. There are no Israeli casualties," the army said in a statement.
Israel says it killed two guerrillas in Lebanon

The army said the raid north of Israel's 15 km (nine mile) -wide south Lebanon occupation zone was a lesson to guerrillas they could not act with impunity against Israeli troops and their client South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia.

"The hit against the terrorists in the outskirts of the villages used as launching bases for operations against the army and SLA clarifies the army will not allow terrorist operations in the villages and their environs, something that contradicts the Grapes of Wrath understandings," the army statement said.

Grapes of Wrath was the code name for the Israeli blitz against guerrillas in Lebanon a year ago that killed some 200 Lebanese, most civilians. No Israelis were killed though some 50 were wounded by guerrilla rockets launched at northern Israel.

The blitz ended with U.S.-brokered understandings barring the sides from attacking civilians or using them for cover. On Sunday, one SLA man was killed and two others wounded by a roadside bomb Hizbollah said its men planted.
